title: Reviewer correction
description: What a reviewer changed about a proposed response, pinned to the exact run that produced it. Factory turns an APPROVED correction into a test or a proposed skill change; it never alters production behaviour on its own. The kit does not collect corrections - Body does - but the kit defines the shape, because the kit owns what a case is. The pinning in `correction_of` is what makes a correction replayable: a correction that cannot be tied to an input and a skill version cannot become a regression test, only an anecdote.

correction_of.description: The run this corrects. Every field comes from that run's _report/run_manifest.json and none may be omitted: a correction that does not name the skill version it corrects can be replayed against the wrong one and 'pass'.

engine_commit.description: The manifest's engine.source_commit, or "" when that run could not attribute the engine. Empty string rather than null: the kit's own schema engine supports neither union types nor a general oneOf (its oneOf is a hard-coded `source` discriminator for the kit manifest), and a correction contract that the kit cannot machine-check would be a contract in name only. See FOLLOW-UP-10.

input_sha256.description: The manifest's input.sha256, or "" when it could not be read.

artifact.description: Which document the reviewer was looking at.

original.description: The kit's proposal, verbatim. Checked byte-for-byte against what the run actually produced, so a correction cannot claim the kit said something it did not.

corrected.description: What the reviewer sent instead, verbatim.

reason.description: Why, in the reviewer's words. Required: a diff without a reason is not knowledge, and Factory cannot turn it into a test that means anything.

disposition.description: case_specific - true of this case only, and must NOT become a rule. reusable_knowledge - the reviewer proposes it as company knowledge, which still requires approval before Factory acts on it.
